news.headline: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis
news.story_lead: Vanessa Trump and her 19-year-old daughter Kai - Published 1 hour ago Vanessa Trump, the former wife of Donald Trump Jr, has announced that she is cancer-free following her breast cancer diagnosis earlier this year. Trump, 48, who has five children with President Donald Trump's eldest son, shared in a short video on her 19-year-old daughter Kai's Instagram account that her recent tests results "came back clear, so I'm finally cancer-free". The video, posted on Friday, teases the release of a longer YouTube video to come on Saturday, in which Vanessa and Kai Trump will discuss breast cancer awareness and prevention, Kai wrote in the caption.
news.full_article_text: Vanessa Trump and her 19-year-old daughter Kai - Published 1 hour ago Vanessa Trump, the former wife of Donald Trump Jr, has announced that she is cancer-free following her breast cancer diagnosis earlier this year. Trump, 48, who has five children with President Donald Trump's eldest son, shared in a short video on her 19-year-old daughter Kai's Instagram account that her recent tests results "came back clear, so I'm finally cancer-free". The video, posted on Friday, teases the release of a longer YouTube video to come on Saturday, in which Vanessa and Kai Trump will discuss breast cancer awareness and prevention, Kai wrote in the caption. Vanessa Trump separated from Trump Jr in 2018 and announced last year that she had begun dating US pro golfer Tiger Woods. "October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a time to raise awareness about early detection, education, and support for those affected by breast cancer," Kai Trump wrote on Instagram. "I sat down with my mom and Dr. Nicole Saphier to talk about my mom's journey with breast cancer and learn more about prevention and early detection," she continued. Kai's post received over 20,000 likes and hundreds of comments from people offering support and well wishes, including from American singer and media personality Mary Millben. In Friday's video, Trump said she was first diagnosed with breast cancer in April. She publicly announced the diagnosis in May, saying in a social media post that she had undergone surgery and was working on a treatment plan with her medical team. According to the American Cancer Society, the average risk of a woman in the US developing breast cancer is about 1 in 8, or 13%. The disease also accounts for 30% of all new female cancers every year, according to the group. Surgery cures most breast cancers, but if some disease remains, chemotherapy, radiotherapy and endocrine therapy can reduce the long-term risk. Treatments have been advancing, including more targeted therapies for early breast cancer, new types of hormonal therapies, and more precise and effective radiotherapy. news.headline: Farooq Abdullah's remarks on Pakistan, Kashmiris spark row; BJP demands apology
news.story_lead: Farooq Abdullah's remarks on Pakistan, Kashmiris spark row; BJP demands apology The former Jammu and Kashmir CM made the remarks at a party event in Baramulla district of Kashmir Valley. Former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Farooq Abdullah set off a political row with his alleged pro-Pakistan remarks made at a rally in Baramulla district of Kashmir Valley on Saturday. The J&K unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) sought an apology from Abdullah, who is also the chief of J&K National Conference party, over the controversial remarks.
news.full_article_text: Farooq Abdullah's remarks on Pakistan, Kashmiris spark row; BJP demands apology The former Jammu and Kashmir CM made the remarks at a party event in Baramulla district of Kashmir Valley. Former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Farooq Abdullah set off a political row with his alleged pro-Pakistan remarks made at a rally in Baramulla district of Kashmir Valley on Saturday. The J&K unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) sought an apology from Abdullah, who is also the chief of J&K National Conference party, over the controversial remarks. Without naming Pakistan, Abdullah said that the 'neighbour’ is protecting Kashmir. He said there is little hope for Kashmiris from the Centre and urged Kashmiris to have courage to confront Delhi. "If you don't keep it, you will be erased. Even our trace and identity will disappear. Nothing will be left. They are silent today because there is noise in the world, and our neighbour is constantly behind this. Everywhere they say, 'the decision regarding Kashmir has not been made'. That is what is saving us. Otherwise, their intentions are not good," he said. He further asserted that the people of J&K never denied being Indians. "We never said that we are not Indians. Time and time again, we affirmed that we acceded to India - to the India of Mahatma Gandhi, the India of Jawaharlal Nehru, the India of (Maulana Abul Kalam) Azad," he said. He alleged that Muslims and Hindus are being pitted against each other for ‘power’. "India's fabric was destroyed; we never imagined this would happen. But this too shall end, God willing; its time will come," Abdullah was quoted as saying by news agency PTI . BJP seeks apology The remarks kicked up a row with BJP's J&K president Sat Sharma demanding an apology from the former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister. “Farooq Abdullah needs to understand that he has the freedom to say whatever he wishes in this country. It is precisely because of this freedom that he is able to make such statements. Had you made these remarks in Pakistan, you might not have been spared,” Sharma said, adding that Article 370 was imposed on the state. Also read: JDU expels Mokama MLA Anant Singh from party for 6 years, days after controversial remarks spark row “The rights of women were taken away. Today, Muslims across the country, including those in Jammu and Kashmir, understand the situation. Muslims in Jammu and Kashmir know that they are safe in the hands of India...The Bharatiya Janata Party will not tolerate such conduct. He should publicly apologise to the people of India. Otherwise, I would say that Pakistan would be a better place for him, and he should go and settle there,” he added. Former union minister Arjun Munda also condemned Abdullah's remarks, saying that such a statement, if made by a former chief minister, was unfortunate and reflected his view of the country. "If such a statement has come from him, then it becomes self-evident how he views this country. Today, that is clearly reflected in his statements. I did not expect his statements to take such a form, but since they have, it is not just saddening; it is condemnable,” Munda was quoted as saying by news agency ANI . Uttar Pradesh minister Suresh Kumar Khanna accused Abdullah of exploiting Kashmiris throughout his political career. He said that the region's integration into the national mainstream under the Modi government was in the best interests of its people. “It is people like Farooq Abdullah who have exploited Kashmir throughout their lives. Farooq Abdullah is responsible for reducing Kashmiris to second-class citizens, and he ought not to be making such statements. It is precisely because of India’s diversity that Kashmir is now integrated into the nation’s mainstream, and every citizen of Kashmir enjoys the same rights as those in the rest of India," Khanna was quoted as saying. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR HT News Desk Follow the latest breaking news, major developments and agenda-setting stories from India and around the world with the newsdesk at Hindustan Times. news.exam_corner_topic: Amit Shah visits Delhi Police headquarters to take stock of law and order in national capital
news.headline: Amit Shah visits Delhi Police headquarters to take stock of law and order in national capital
news.story_lead: Amit Shah visits Delhi Police headquarters to take stock of law and order in national capital Amit Shah’s visit to Delhi Police headquarters comes amid scrutiny of the force’s handling of a July protest. Union home minister Amit Shah reached the Delhi Police headquarters on Saturday afternoon to take stock of the law and order situation in the national capital, officials said. The recent protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), the fight against drugs, action against gangsters operating from abroad and crimes against women were likely to figure in Shah's discussions with senior officers, police sources said.
news.full_article_text: Amit Shah visits Delhi Police headquarters to take stock of law and order in national capital Amit Shah’s visit to Delhi Police headquarters comes amid scrutiny of the force’s handling of a July protest. Union home minister Amit Shah reached the Delhi Police headquarters on Saturday afternoon to take stock of the law and order situation in the national capital, officials said. The recent protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), the fight against drugs, action against gangsters operating from abroad and crimes against women were likely to figure in Shah's discussions with senior officers, police sources said. Shah reached the police headquarters on Jai Singh Road around 3 pm, where senior officers were expected to brief him on the force's performance, ongoing investigations and key law enforcement challenges, they said. Also Read | Annamalai says CJP has right to protest in India, disagrees with its tactics The visit comes amid heightened scrutiny of the Delhi Police over allegations of using excessive force against protesters during the CJP's 'Sansad Chalo' march in July. The meeting was expected to review the circumstances surrounding the protest, the police response and measures taken to prevent similar incidents in the future, the sources said. The home minister's visit is also expected to boost the morale of the force, which has been under fire of late over its handling of protests, they said. Also Read | 'Let's see what happens': CJP's Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka appear at SEM court days after release Shah's visit marks his return to the Delhi Police headquarters after more than four years. He last visited the police headquarters on August 30, 2022. The meeting is also expected to focus on the government's key priorities, including curbing drug trafficking, dismantling criminal networks of gangsters based overseas, and strengthening action against crimes targeting women, the sources said.

news.story_lead: Delhi court orders trial of Yasin Malik, Engineer Rashid, 5 others in terror funding case The court in September held that sufficient material existed to raise a “strong suspicion” against all accused for an offence under PMLA. A Delhi court on Friday ordered the commencement of trial against jailed Kashmiri separatist leader Yasin Malik , Baramulla MP Sheikh Abdul Rashid, alias Engineer Rashid, and five others in an alleged ₹ 8.94 crore terror-funding and money laundering case linked to Pakistan-based hawala channels. Special Judge Prashant Sharma of Rouse Avenue courts, formally framing charges against the accused, directed that the recording of prosecution evidence will begin on November 19.
news.full_article_text: Delhi court orders trial of Yasin Malik, Engineer Rashid, 5 others in terror funding case The court in September held that sufficient material existed to raise a “strong suspicion” against all accused for an offence under PMLA. A Delhi court on Friday ordered the commencement of trial against jailed Kashmiri separatist leader Yasin Malik , Baramulla MP Sheikh Abdul Rashid, alias Engineer Rashid, and five others in an alleged ₹ 8.94 crore terror-funding and money laundering case linked to Pakistan-based hawala channels. Special Judge Prashant Sharma of Rouse Avenue courts, formally framing charges against the accused, directed that the recording of prosecution evidence will begin on November 19. Also read: Farooq Abdullah's remarks on Pakistan, Kashmiris spark row; BJP demands apology The development came after the court on September 9 ordered framing of charges against the accused, observing that there was sufficient prima facie material on record to raise a "strong suspicion" regarding the involvement of the accused in generating, receiving, and laundering proceeds of crime to fund secessionist activities in Jammu and Kashmir. Yasin Malik pleaded ‘not guilty’ The proceedings were conducted in an in-camera hearing. Appearing through video conferencing from Tihar Jail, Jammu and Kashmir Liberation Front (JKLF) chief Yasin Malik pleaded not guilty to the charges under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) and stated that he would contest the case. The court had in September held that sufficient material existed to raise a “strong suspicion” against all seven accused for an offence under Section 3 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). Also read: JDU expels Mokama MLA Anant Singh from party for 6 years, days after controversial remarks spark row “I conclude that prima facie, there is sufficient material on record based upon which strong suspicion is raised against all seven accused persons,” the special judge had said. The accused in the case are Malik, Zahoor Ahmad Shah Watali, Abdul Rashid Sheikh, Shabir Ahmad Shah, Masarat Alam, Naval Kishore Kapoor and Trison Farms and Constructions Pvt Ltd. What the Enforcement Directorate said According to ED, the criminal activities under investigation generated proceeds of crime totalling ₹ 8.94 crore. The agency alleged that the money was subsequently received, transferred, concealed, possessed, acquired and used by the accused through different channels. ED alleged that funds were allegedly moved through cash couriers from the Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi to members of the Hurriyat leadership, including Malik, to promote the secessionist agenda and support subversive activities. Also read: Demand for students' union, row over ‘slogans’ trigger tensions in Jamia Millia Islamia The agency also relied on material recovered from Ghulam Mohd Bhat, an accountant-cum-cashier working with Watali. The documents allegedly showed that Malik, Shabir Shah and Masarat Alam received foreign contributions through Watali during the 2015-16 financial year. The investigation further uncovered emails associated with Malik which, according to ED, indicated that he had developed a network to raise funds abroad for terrorist, secessionist and unlawful activities in J&K in the name of a “freedom struggle”. The agency alleged these funds were used to sustain the JKLF and intensify secessionist violence. ED had further alleged that Malik received another ₹ 15 lakh through Watali during 2015-16, bringing the total amount allegedly received by Malik to ₹ 30.75 lakh. Malik received ₹ 15 lakh from Saudi in 2013 The National Investigation Agency (NIA), in its second supplementary charge sheet, alleged that Malik had received ₹ 15.75 lakh from Saudi Arabia in 2013. ED treated these amounts as proceeds of crime allegedly derived from criminal activity connected with the scheduled offences. The money laundering proceedings are linked to an NIA case registered in 2017 over an alleged larger conspiracy involving terrorist and secessionist activities in J&K. NIA invoked provisions including criminal conspiracy, 121 (waging war against the government) and 121A (criminal conspiracy against the state) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and sections of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. ED registered its case on June 14, 2017, to investigate the alleged laundering of proceeds generated through those criminal activities. Its main prosecution complaint was filed in 2020, while a supplementary complaint in January 2023 arraigned Malik as an accused. NIA had alleged that Malik was involved in terrorist and subversive activities in the Valley and in raising and receiving funds through illegal channels, including Hawala. The underlying NIA case ultimately resulted in Malik’s conviction in 2022. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Arnabjit Sur Arnabjit Sur is a Senior Correspondent with Hindustan Times who primarily covers stories from the capital's trial courts. news.headline: Centre directs states, UTs to enforce ban on reuse of single-use medical devices
news.story_lead: Centre directs states, UTs to enforce ban on reuse of single-use medical devices The Centre said the practice raised concerns relating to patient safety, infection prevention and control, regulatory compliance and healthcare expenditure. The Centre has directed states and Union Territories to strictly enforce a ban on the reuse of single-use medical devices and disposable surgical items in public and private healthcare facilities, citing infection risks and instances of patients being charged the full cost of reused equipment. In a letter dated October 16, the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) said it had come to its notice that certain private and corporate hospitals were sterilising and reusing devices meant for one-time use, particularly in critical specialities such as cardiology, nephrology, oncology, cardiothoracic and vascular surgery, and neurosurgery .
news.full_article_text: Centre directs states, UTs to enforce ban on reuse of single-use medical devices The Centre said the practice raised concerns relating to patient safety, infection prevention and control, regulatory compliance and healthcare expenditure. The Centre has directed states and Union Territories to strictly enforce a ban on the reuse of single-use medical devices and disposable surgical items in public and private healthcare facilities, citing infection risks and instances of patients being charged the full cost of reused equipment. In a letter dated October 16, the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) said it had come to its notice that certain private and corporate hospitals were sterilising and reusing devices meant for one-time use, particularly in critical specialities such as cardiology, nephrology, oncology, cardiothoracic and vascular surgery, and neurosurgery . "It has been observed that such devices and disposable surgical items, after being used for one procedure, are being subjected to sterilisation and subsequently reused, despite being designated for single use only," the letter said. The DGHS said the practice raised concerns relating to patient safety, infection prevention and control, regulatory compliance and healthcare expenditure. It also flagged instances in which patients were allegedly charged the full cost of these devices despite their reuse, or the cost was reimbursed by the concerned government authorities. Also Read: Emerging era of software as medical device Devices reportedly being reused include cardiac catheters, guidewires, balloon and ablation catheters, introducer sheaths, dialysis equipment such as dialysers and blood tubing, surgical staplers, laparoscopic trocars and orthopaedic drill bits. Syringes and needles have also been identified among items being reused, according to the Association of Indian Medical Device Industry (AiMeD). Even after sterilisation , devices designed for one-time use may not be safe for reuse, as inadequate reprocessing or deterioration can compromise their performance and leave biological material behind, the directorate said. The practice could expose patients to cross-infections, device malfunction, reduced performance and other procedure-related complications, the DGHS warned. These infections may include hepatitis B and C, HIV and bacterial infections. The directorate said the practice could violate provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act , 1940, the Medical Devices Rules, 2017, the Clinical Establishments Act, 2010, and applicable infection prevention and biomedical waste management requirements. "It has accordingly been decided that the reuse of single-use medical devices and disposable surgical items shall be strictly prohibited in all healthcare organisations, including both public and private healthcare facilities, under the administrative jurisdiction of the Government of India , states and Union Territories," the letter said. The DGHS has asked chief secretaries, state health department officials, directors of health services, the Drug Controller General of India (DCGI) and state and UT drug controllers to ensure strict vigilance and effective enforcement. Authorities have been asked to inspect and monitor healthcare establishments, ensure compliance with the directive and take appropriate action in cases of violations. "All single-use devices/disposable surgical items should be utilised strictly in accordance with the instructions and recommendations of the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM)," the letter said. The letter also referred to a Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS) office memorandum issued in December 2016 concerning the reuse of such devices in hospitals empanelled under the scheme.

news.headline: Odisha doctor who served tribals arrested; police allege instigation, Congress slams ‘anti-mining crackdown’
news.story_lead: Odisha doctor who served tribals arrested; police allege instigation, Congress slams ‘anti-mining crackdown’ Randall Sequeira, a doctor and tribal rights activist, and Dalit activist Laxman Naik were arrested on the night of October 16 in Odisha. A doctor who moved to Odisha to improve healthcare access for tribal communities has reportedly been arrested in connection with a clash during protests against bauxite mining in the state. The Congress has attacked the BJP over the arrest of Randall Sequeira, 39, and Dalit activist Laxman Naik, alleging a wider crackdown on tribals and Dalit communities opposing mining projects.
news.full_article_text: Odisha doctor who served tribals arrested; police allege instigation, Congress slams ‘anti-mining crackdown’ Randall Sequeira, a doctor and tribal rights activist, and Dalit activist Laxman Naik were arrested on the night of October 16 in Odisha. A doctor who moved to Odisha to improve healthcare access for tribal communities has reportedly been arrested in connection with a clash during protests against bauxite mining in the state. The Congress has attacked the BJP over the arrest of Randall Sequeira, 39, and Dalit activist Laxman Naik, alleging a wider crackdown on tribals and Dalit communities opposing mining projects. Randall Sequeira, 39, a doctor who moved to Odisha to improve healthcare access for adivasi communities, and Dalit activist Laxman Naik were arrested on the night of October 16 in connection with a clash between locals and police in Kantamal village in Rayagada district in April, news agency PTI reported. Both have been charged with serious criminal offences, including attempt to murder and rioting, and booked under the Arms Act , a senior police officer told PTI . The police have rejected allegations that the arrests were intended to suppress protests, claiming that the two had instigated tribals to attack security personnel during a protest against mining activities. Also Read: 2 tribal rights activists held for 'involvement' in clash in Odisha, civil society group condemns Police say activists instigated tribals South Western Range DIG Akhileshvar Singh rejected the allegations of repression. "The arrested persons were not innocent. Dr Randall Sequeira was not providing medical services to the people but was engaged in instigating tribals against the state government. Naik was also misleading people. Why do police arrest any innocent person, especially a doctor?" Singh told PTI. Who is Randall Sequeira? Originally from Mangaluru, Karnataka, Sequeira grew up in Mumbai, where he completed his schooling. He completed his MBBS at St John’s Medical College in Bengaluru and an MD in internal medicine at Sawai Man Singh Medical College and Hospital in Rajasthan, according to his LinkedIn profile. In 2017, he moved to Kalahandi to work with NGOs operating in the tribal region. After a few years, he began working independently, travelling to remote villages to treat tribal communities and understand their living conditions, The Indian Express reported. Alongside his healthcare work, Sequeira supported protests against bauxite mining in the region. In September 2023, Kashipur police in Rayagada district made a general diary entry concerning the circulation of pamphlets, maps and anti-mining material in villages around the Sijimali hills, a proposed bauxite mining site, The Indian Express reported. Who is Laxman Naik? Naik is a leading Dalit activist associated with the Ma Mati Mali Surakhya Manch and Samajwadi Jan Parishad, PTI reported. The Concerned Citizens Committee, Odisha, said both activists supported people’s movements against the distress caused by mining and industrialisation and worked to protect human habitats. The civil society organisation condemned the arrests, alleging that the two were taken into custody with the “sole intention to foil the tribals' fight against injustice and for their rights over natural resources like 'Jal, Jangal & Jameen' (water, forest and land)”. Congress alleges wider crackdown Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh said Odisha Police picked up Sequeira and Naik on October 16 because they had supported protests by tribal and Dalit communities against bauxite mining projects. "They have been supporting protests by Dalit and tribal communities against Bauxite mining projects. This is part of a larger campaign of repression in Odisha which has seen 43 police cases and over a 100 people jailed in three years," he alleged. Congress MP from Koraput Saptagiri Ulaka and the Odisha Congress are supporting the arrested activists, Ramesh said. He alleged that mining projects in Sijimali, Kutrumali and Niyamgiri were being pushed through in violation of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996, and the Forest Rights Act, 2006, despite the areas falling under the Fifth Schedule. Ramesh also claimed there were serious allegations of forged gram sabha consent in Sijimali and criticised the Centre’s environmental clearance for the project. "This is the double engine model at work denying tribal communities their rights," he said. According to The Indian Express , the clash took place on April 7 after a pre-dawn police raid in Kantamal amid opposition to the construction of an approach road to the Sijimali bauxite reserve. Villagers alleged that police entered the village to detain people opposing the road project, while police said they had gone to arrest a person against whom a non-bailable warrant had been issued. Nearly 58 people, including police personnel, sustained injuries in the clash, and 23 activists and local residents were arrested. Before moving into this role, she worked with the Bengaluru desk, where she extensively covered civic issues, Karnataka politics, infrastructure, and urban governance. Over the past seven years, Anagha has worked across multiple facets of digital journalism, including reporting, editing, and video production. She briefly stepped away from journalism, only to realize that the newsroom is where she has the most fun. Her interests lie in tracking national and state politics, particularly South Indian politics, as well as social issues and public policy. She has previously worked with Deccan Herald, Mid-day, The Federal, and ThePrint, and has lived and worked in Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, and Chennai. A doctor who moved to Odisha to improve healthcare access for tribal communities has reportedly been arrested in connection with a clash during protests against bauxite mining in the state. The Congress has attacked the BJP over the arrest of Randall Sequeira, 39, and Dalit activist Laxman Naik, alleging a wider crackdown on tribals and Dalit communities opposing mining projects. Randall Sequeira, 39, a doctor who moved to Odisha to improve healthcare access for adivasi communities, and Dalit activist Laxman Naik were arrested on the night of October 16 in connection with a clash between locals and police in Kantamal village in Rayagada district in April, news agency PTI reported. Both have been charged with serious criminal offences, including attempt to murder and rioting, and booked under the Arms Act , a senior police officer told PTI . The police have rejected allegations that the arrests were intended to suppress protests, claiming that the two had instigated tribals to attack security personnel during a protest against mining activities. Also Read: 2 tribal rights activists held for 'involvement' in clash in Odisha, civil society group condemns Police say activists instigated tribals South Western Range DIG Akhileshvar Singh rejected the allegations of repression. "The arrested persons were not innocent. Dr Randall Sequeira was not providing medical services to the people but was engaged in instigating tribals against the state government. Naik was also misleading people. Why do police arrest any innocent person, especially a doctor?" Singh told PTI. Who is Randall Sequeira? Originally from Mangaluru, Karnataka, Sequeira grew up in Mumbai, where he completed his schooling. He completed his MBBS at St John’s Medical College in Bengaluru and an MD in internal medicine at Sawai Man Singh Medical College and Hospital in Rajasthan, according to his LinkedIn profile. In 2017, he moved to Kalahandi to work with NGOs operating in the tribal region. After a few years, he began working independently, travelling to remote villages to treat tribal communities and understand their living conditions, The Indian Express reported. Alongside his healthcare work, Sequeira supported protests against bauxite mining in the region. In September 2023, Kashipur police in Rayagada district made a general diary entry concerning the circulation of pamphlets, maps and anti-mining material in villages around the Sijimali hills, a proposed bauxite mining site, The Indian Express reported. Who is Laxman Naik? Naik is a leading Dalit activist associated with the Ma Mati Mali Surakhya Manch and Samajwadi Jan Parishad, PTI reported. The Concerned Citizens Committee, Odisha, said both activists supported people’s movements against the distress caused by mining and industrialisation and worked to protect human habitats. The civil society organisation condemned the arrests, alleging that the two were taken into custody with the “sole intention to foil the tribals' fight against injustice and for their rights over natural resources like 'Jal, Jangal & Jameen' (water, forest and land)”. Congress alleges wider crackdown Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh said Odisha Police picked up Sequeira and Naik on October 16 because they had supported protests by tribal and Dalit communities against bauxite mining projects. "They have been supporting protests by Dalit and tribal communities against Bauxite mining projects. This is part of a larger campaign of repression in Odisha which has seen 43 police cases and over a 100 people jailed in three years," he alleged. Congress MP from Koraput Saptagiri Ulaka and the Odisha Congress are supporting the arrested activists, Ramesh said. He alleged that mining projects in Sijimali, Kutrumali and Niyamgiri were being pushed through in violation of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996, and the Forest Rights Act, 2006, despite the areas falling under the Fifth Schedule. Ramesh also claimed there were serious allegations of forged gram sabha consent in Sijimali and criticised the Centre’s environmental clearance for the project. "This is the double engine model at work denying tribal communities their rights," he said. According to The Indian Express , the clash took place on April 7 after a pre-dawn police raid in Kantamal amid opposition to the construction of an approach road to the Sijimali bauxite reserve. Villagers alleged that police entered the village to detain people opposing the road project, while police said they had gone to arrest a person against whom a non-bailable warrant had been issued. Nearly 58 people, including police personnel, sustained injuries in the clash, and 23 activists and local residents were arrested. Before moving into this role, she worked with the Bengaluru desk, where she extensively covered civic issues, Karnataka politics, infrastructure, and urban governance. Over the past seven years, Anagha has worked across multiple facets of digital journalism, including reporting, editing, and video production. She briefly stepped away from journalism, only to realize that the newsroom is where she has the most fun. Her interests lie in tracking national and state politics, particularly South Indian politics, as well as social issues and public policy. She has previously worked with Deccan Herald, Mid-day, The Federal, and ThePrint, and has lived and worked in Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, and Chennai. news.headline: Student movement takes Serbia's Vučić to the wire in neck-and-neck election

Ilija SrdanoviÄ appears an unlikely opponent for Serbia's long-serving leader, Aleksandar VuÄiÄ, arriving for an interview by motorbike sporting a fluorescent yellow jacket emblazoned with pro-student slogans. He has been selected as top candidate for an opposition movement posing the most serious challenge to VuÄiÄ since the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) entered government in 2012.
news.full_article_text: The Student List is Number 3 on Serbia's ballot paper, so the figure seen being hugged by this supporter has become a symbol of the movement's fight for change - Published 24 October 2026, 00:08 BST If Sunday's parliamentary elections really are a battle for the heart of Serbia, then who better than a cardiologist to be one of the leading figures in the race. Ilija SrdanoviÄ appears an unlikely opponent for Serbia's long-serving leader, Aleksandar VuÄiÄ, arriving for an interview by motorbike sporting a fluorescent yellow jacket emblazoned with pro-student slogans. He has been selected as top candidate for an opposition movement posing the most serious challenge to VuÄiÄ since the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) entered government in 2012. The Student List has emerged from almost two years of anti-corruption protests led by young Serbians, outraged by the deaths of 16 people when a railway station's canopy collapsed in Serbia's second city Novi Sad. - What you need to know about Serbia's pivotal election Published 1 day ago Instead of running for office themselves, student-led assemblies at the country's university faculties have chosen 250 candidates to stand in the parliamentary election, with SrdanoviÄ, professor at Novi Sad University, heading the list. "It is absolutely normal to stand with my students to help them in their fair struggle," SrdanoviÄ told the BBC. Ilija SrdanoviÄ tops the Student List's 250 candidates but would not necessarily lead Serbia if they won The Student List is up against a Serbian leader who has served successively as deputy prime minister, prime minister and president since 2012. When he called these snap elections last month , he stood down as president to run again for the role of prime minister. Whatever VuÄiÄ's title, there has never been any doubt that he was the man in charge â an image enthusiastically promoted by Serbia's largely uncritical media. He retains strong support among a significant section of Serbia's population. They view him as a strong leader who stands up for the country's interests. He can also point to significant economic growth over the past decade and numerous improvements in infrastructure. VuÄiÄ has painted the student movement as foreign-backed and seeking to "bring down our state". "Let us always protect and defend it," he told supporters at a final campaign rally. Just like the protest movement from which it developed, the Student List has no hierarchy or nominated leader. This makes it a proposition unlike any other in Serbia's relatively short democratic history. Reliable polls are thin on the ground, but analysts are predicting an extremely tight vote. A reported 150,000 supporters turned out for the final Student List rally in Belgrade's Slavija Square on Thursday night Ilija SrdanoviÄ may head the list of candidates â but he is not the movement's leader and would not necessarily be first choice prime minister if they won. SrdanoviÄ insists that the Student List has a clear vision: "We offer to our citizens the core values of civilised society, which this previous regime has taken away from our citizens for the last time." The other candidates on the Student List range from academics to athletes â and economists to engineers. None of them has a political background. But the students who selected them believe that is a strength, rather than a weakness. "We've gathered people who are actually the best in their fields, and we really think that they are competent enough to rule the country," says Aleksandra, a student at Novi Sad University who only wants to give her first name. "All of them are gathered around the same vision of a country where the freedom of speech is ruling, where you can walk to your home in the middle of the night and you will not be beaten up by some hooligans," she adds. The Student List and its supporters say that Aleksandar VuÄiÄ and the SNS dominate state institutions and media coverage. At the last parliamentary election in 2023, the International Election Observation Mission noted "overwhelming ruling party advantage" due to "bias in the media" and "misuse of public office and resources". The BBC approached leading figures in the SNS for an interview but was not offered a response. VuÄiÄ continues to command strong support among sections of Serbia's population For the past 18 months, there has also been a full-time, pro-SNS camp in the small park between the National Assembly and the Presidency building in the centre of Belgrade. Its residents have repeatedly attacked journalists and made the park a no-go zone for local people. VuÄiÄ has called the camp "a symbol of resistance" against those who "cannot stand different opinions". But his major challenge remains what happened outside Novi Sad railway station two years ago. The station's renovation was a key part of his signature infrastructure project â the high-speed line linking Belgrade and Budapest. So it has been difficult for VuÄiÄ to distance himself from the disaster. Aleksandar VuÄiÄ stepped down as president last month with the aim of returning to the post of prime minister Protests followed, with participants accusing the authorities of corruption and having "blood on their hands". "This is a problem for the government," says Magda Anastasijevic, the Eastern Europe analyst for the conflict monitor, ACLED. "VuÄiÄ has survived this in the past, he was always able to find a scapegoat and blame whatever problems on them. This was not the case for the canopy." On the diplomatic front, he has performed a delicate balancing act. Membership talks with the EU continue, albeit fitfully, even as Serbia retains close ties with Russia and China â both countries that refuse to recognise Kosovo's unilateral declaration of independence from Serbia. VuÄiÄ has warned those links could be severed if the Student List took power. "When you ask them: will you impose sanctions on Russia? Silence, umming and ah-ing, but no answer," he told the audience at a pre-election rally. "You know what the Chinese think, you've heard what Vladimir Putin said. So you decide. Think about who has our best interests at heart." The final rallies of the campaign saw the SNS stage an event at Belgrade Arena, with Aleksandar VuÄiÄ as the only speaker. But on the other side of the Sava River, the Student List attracted a reported 150,000 people in Slavija Square to listen to a mixture of students and candidates. The contrasting visions were clear to see: the strong, sole leader â or a collective approach. Now Serbia's electorate must decide which they prefer. Related topics

news.exam_corner_topic: Supreme Court orders Rajasthan to seal illegal discharge points into polluted rivers, recover fines
news.headline: Supreme Court orders Rajasthan to seal illegal discharge points into polluted rivers, recover fines
news.story_lead: Supreme Court orders Rajasthan to seal illegal discharge points into polluted rivers, recover fines The Supreme Court has directed Rajasthan to seal illegal discharge points polluting the Jojari-Luni-Bandi river system and recover environmental compensation for the entire period of violations. The Supreme Court has directed the Rajasthan government to seal and dismantle all illegal discharge points into the Jojari-Luni-Bandi river system and recover environmental compensation from polluters for the entire period of violations, while calling for a shift from a reactive to a proactive approach to tackling environmental damage. The directions form part of suo motu proceedings initiated by the court last year after a news report highlighted alarming levels of pollution in the Jojari river, which serves as a lifeline for a population of 2 million in the state.
news.full_article_text: Supreme Court orders Rajasthan to seal illegal discharge points into polluted rivers, recover fines The Supreme Court has directed Rajasthan to seal illegal discharge points polluting the Jojari-Luni-Bandi river system and recover environmental compensation for the entire period of violations. The Supreme Court has directed the Rajasthan government to seal and dismantle all illegal discharge points into the Jojari-Luni-Bandi river system and recover environmental compensation from polluters for the entire period of violations, while calling for a shift from a reactive to a proactive approach to tackling environmental damage. The directions form part of suo motu proceedings initiated by the court last year after a news report highlighted alarming levels of pollution in the Jojari river, which serves as a lifeline for a population of 2 million in the state. In its order issued on September 29 and uploaded recently, the court directed the state government to “seal and dismantle” all illegal and unauthorised discharge points into the river, including bypass arrangements, manholes, chambers, pipelines and conduits. The concerned state authorities were also directed to initiate appropriate proceedings against the landowners or occupiers and state officials responsible for the lapses. The order further directed the Rajasthan State Pollution Control Board (RSPCB) to “initiate proceedings for assessment, imposition and actual recovery of Environmental Compensation” for the entire period of the violations from the industrial units, persons or entities that benefited from them. The court said environmental issues did not merit an incident-based response in which the state bureaucracy reacts only after a violation is reported. It called for a “fundamental shift” in the approach, requiring the state machinery to anticipate potential environmental risks and act proactively. The bench of justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said, “There is a dire need for a fundamental change in the manner in which the bureaucracy approaches these issues.” It added, “The state machinery must shed its traditional reactive posture, move away from a practice of responding only after violations are brought to its notice, and bring about an internal reorientation in its functioning so as to anticipate environmental risks, act proactively and ensure continuous coordination amongst the concerned authorities.” The latest order is part of a series of directions issued by the court over the past few months to halt industrial activities along the three rivers, strengthen common effluent treatment plants (CETPs) and prevent industrial waste from being discharged directly into the river system. Survey of bridges, road crossings To maintain the natural flow of the rivers, the court directed the Rajasthan government and the concerned authorities to undertake a “comprehensive technical survey” of all bridges and road crossings across the Luni, Jojari and Bandi river systems and their tributaries. The survey will identify structures that impede or could impede the rivers’ natural flow. The state was also directed to remove such obstructions and put safeguards in place to prevent future construction that could disrupt the flow. Action against illegal sand mining The court also focused on river sand mining, another potential impediment to the natural flow of the rivers. A nine-member committee headed by former Rajasthan high court judge justice (retd) Sangeet Lodha, which is assisting the court in efforts to improve the Jojari-Luni-Bandi river ecosystems, said it had sought information from state authorities on existing sand mining leases, the quantity of sand mined and restoration obligations. However, the information had not been provided to the committee so far. The bench directed the state and the concerned authorities to take immediate and effective enforcement action against “all illegal and unauthorised Bajari/sand mining activities which have an adverse impact upon the riverbed, riverbanks or the natural flow and ecology of the river system.” The state chief secretary was directed to provide the committee with details of permitted and illegal mining areas, mining leases, quantities extracted, replenishment and mining depths, among other information. The court also directed the state to establish a permanent, district-wise and coordinated enforcement mechanism involving the RSPCB, district administration, police, revenue, transport, local bodies and other concerned agencies. The mechanism must designate nodal officers for regular field surveillance and interdepartmental coordination to ensure prompt action when illegal industrial activities are identified. Single-window mechanism for CETPs The court directed the state chief secretary to ensure that all pending proposals relating to Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs) and their upgradation to zero liquid discharge (ZLD) are processed and decided through a single-window or designated nodal mechanism. This would facilitate the simultaneous technical, financial and statutory processing of the proposals. After examining the justice Lodha committee’s report, the bench said the challenges facing the Jojari-Bandi-Luni river ecosystem stemmed from several factors. These included inadequate treatment capacity, the continued operation of unauthorised industrial activities, ineffective control over land use and discharge mechanisms, insufficient surveillance and enforcement, and interventions that disrupted the rivers’ natural course and flow. “The recurring nature of these concerns, despite the directions issued by this Court from time to time, demonstrates that a purely incident-based response is inadequate,” the court said, directing the state government to submit a further affidavit detailing compliance with its latest directions. The matter is scheduled for hearing on Monday. Earlier directions on construction near rivers In August, the Supreme Court had directed that no construction or development activity be undertaken within 100 metres of the edges of the three rivers. It had also restrained the establishment of hazardous industries or activities within 500 metres on either side of the rivers’ existing flood lines. The court took suo motu cognisance in September 2025 after news reports highlighted severe pollution in the Jojari river, which serves a population of 2 million. It found that sewage and water mixed with industrial effluents had adversely affected crops. Cattle consuming the contaminated water and fodder grown using it had also reportedly suffered health problems, including infertility, miscarriage and skin diseases. In November, the court constituted the justice Lodha committee to propose a River Restoration and Rejuvenation Plan for the Jojari-Luni-Bandi river system. news.exam_corner_topic: Drowning death cannot rule out murder, says Supreme Court, restores trial in boy’s death case
news.headline: Drowning death cannot rule out murder, says Supreme Court, restores trial in boy’s death case
news.story_lead: Drowning death cannot rule out murder, says Supreme Court, restores trial in boy’s death case The Supreme Court has restored murder proceedings in a boy’s drowning death, ruling that a postmortem confirming drowning cannot automatically rule out foul play. A death by drowning cannot automatically be treated as a natural accident, the Supreme Court has held, cautioning that even a postmortem confirming drowning cannot rule out foul play and that the circumstances surrounding the death must be investigated. A bench of justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran set aside a Patna High Court order quashing criminal proceedings against a man accused of murder in the drowning death of a boy, holding that the high court had casually brushed aside compelling circumstances warranting a trial.
news.full_article_text: Drowning death cannot rule out murder, says Supreme Court, restores trial in boy’s death case The Supreme Court has restored murder proceedings in a boy’s drowning death, ruling that a postmortem confirming drowning cannot automatically rule out foul play. A death by drowning cannot automatically be treated as a natural accident, the Supreme Court has held, cautioning that even a postmortem confirming drowning cannot rule out foul play and that the circumstances surrounding the death must be investigated. A bench of justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran set aside a Patna High Court order quashing criminal proceedings against a man accused of murder in the drowning death of a boy, holding that the high court had casually brushed aside compelling circumstances warranting a trial. “Merely because the postmortem indicated death by drowning, it cannot be assumed that there was absolutely no foul play,” said the bench in its recent order, emphasising that even if a person is deliberately pushed into water with the intention of drowning him, a postmortem examination may reveal nothing suspicious. The court was hearing an appeal filed by the boy’s father, challenging the high court’s May decision to quash the taking of cognisance of offences under Sections 302 (murder) and 201 (causing disappearance of evidence) of the Indian Penal Code against the accused. According to the father’s complaint, the accused, Kumar Gitanshu, had taken his son from their home for a walk on May 12, 2020. A short while later, a man informed the family that the boy was drowning near a state boring facility and that, despite his efforts, he could not save him. The father rushed to the spot and arranged for boatmen to search the river, but the efforts proved unsuccessful as the boy had been swept away by the current. The bench noted that two witnesses had also stated that they saw the accused fleeing from the scene. These circumstances, it said, made the case suspicious and warranted a trial to unravel the mystery surrounding the boy’s death. “Especially when the 2nd respondent (accused) who took the deceased from his house, with whom he was last seen, should proffer an explanation, more so, when he was found running away from the spot,” noted the court. The Supreme Court faulted the high court for relying on the postmortem finding that the death was caused by asphyxia and ventricular fibrillation resulting from drowning, treating it as a reason to rule out anything sinister. Such a conclusion, the bench said, failed to account for the possibility that drowning itself could have been the means by which a person was deliberately killed. The court also rejected the high court’s reasoning that the first information report had been lodged after the father received information about the drowning without adequately disclosing how that information reached him. A reading of the FIR, the bench pointed out, clearly showed that the information had been conveyed to the family by the man who reported the incident, following which the father rushed to the spot and arranged a search. “The finding of the High Court is flawed insofar as the documents having not been read properly,” the order said. The case had earlier seen a judicial magistrate accept the police’s final report, which effectively closed the investigation, and direct that the father’s protest petition be registered as a complaint. In revision, a court in Darbhanga directed the magistrate to reconsider the closure report, pointing to circumstances that could justify taking cognisance. On reconsideration, the magistrate took cognisance of the offences. The Patna High Court subsequently quashed that decision, prompting the father to approach the Supreme Court. The top court said the high court had failed to properly examine the detailed revisional order, which had considered statements recorded during the investigation and found prima facie material warranting a trial. Reiterating the law on police closure reports, the bench said a magistrate is not bound to accept the police’s conclusion that no offence has been made out. The court can accept the closure report and end the proceedings, take cognisance on the basis of the material collected, or direct further investigation. “The primacy of the Court to take cognizance or deny it is the law discernible from the very provisions of the CrPC,” said the bench, quoting an earlier Supreme Court judgment.

news.full_article_text:
### RBI Bulletin Findings

According to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Bulletin, the domestic economy is sustained by robust macroeconomic fundamentals and targeted policy measures.

### Key Factual Highlights

* **Macroeconomic Stability:** Sound economic indicators provide resilience and anchor domestic growth.
* **Policy Interventions:** Proactive administrative and regulatory measures implemented by financial authorities continue to support economic activity.
* **Economic Resilience:** Sound fundamentals combined with policy oversight help mitigate headwinds and reinforce long-term stability.

hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### आरबीआई बुलेटिन के मुख्य बिंदु

भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक (आरबीआई) के मासिक बुलेटिन के अनुसार, घरेलू अर्थव्यवस्था को मजबूत समष्टि आर्थिक बुनियादी ढांचों और लक्षित नीतिगत उपायों का समर्थन प्राप्त है।

### प्रमुख तथ्य

* **समष्टि आर्थिक स्थिरता:** मजबूत आर्थिक संकेतक घरेलू विकास को स्थिरता प्रदान करते हैं।
* **नीतिगत सहायता:** वित्तीय अधिकारियों द्वारा उठाए गए सक्रिय प्रशासनिक और नियामक कदम आर्थिक गतिविधियों को समर्थन देना जारी रखते हैं।
* **आर्थिक लचीलापन:** नीतिगत देखरेख और ठोस बुनियादी सिद्धांत मिलकर दीर्घकालिक स्थिरता को सुदृढ़ करते हैं।

“As one of the members of BRICS, Iran reaffirms its commitment to active and effective participation at the highest levels in the summits and meetings of this grouping,” the embassy said in a statement.

“In this regard, the Iranian delegation will continue its dialogue and consultations with delegations from BRICS member countries, with a view to expanding and deepening bilateral and multilateral cooperation, particularly in the field of parliamentary relations and cooperation.”

news.headline: Indo-US Earth Observation Satellite Detected Nepal Disaster Prior to Impact
news.story_lead: A joint $1.3 billion Indo-US satellite detected environmental changes preceding a major natural disaster in Nepal. However, the early indication failed to translate into timely administrative warnings or preventive action on the ground.
news.full_article_text:
### Indo-US Satellite and Disaster Early Warning

Data gathered from a $1.3 billion joint Indo-US Earth observation satellite captured early signals of an impending natural disaster in Nepal before it occurred. Despite advanced sensor capabilities recording these geological or environmental changes, operational early warnings were not effectively communicated, highlighting challenges in disaster management communication networks.

### Key Highlights
* **Mission Scope:** The joint satellite initiative between India and the United States represents a $1.3 billion investment in high-precision Earth observation.
* **Detection Capabilities:** Advanced radar instruments captured surface and environmental changes prior to the disaster hitting Nepal.
* **Communication Gap:** The incident underlines the critical gap between technological detection of hazards by space assets and real-time dissemination of actionable alerts to vulnerable regions.
bullet_points: A $1.3 billion joint Indo-US Earth observation satellite identified precursor signals before a natural disaster occurred in Nepal.
The satellite utilizes advanced radar imagery capable of mapping surface changes and environmental risks.
Despite technical detection, actionable warnings were not processed or transmitted in time to prevent disaster impacts.
The event emphasizes the need to bridge the gap between space technology observations and local emergency response systems.
Effective disaster mitigation relies on fast-tracked data analysis and automated alerting protocols.
key_facts: Estimated cost of the joint satellite: $1.3 billion.
Partner nations: India and the United States.
Affected region: Nepal.
important_dates: 2026-10-24: Reporting date on the satellite's early detection of the disaster in Nepal.
exam_relevance: Prelims: Joint space missions, dual-frequency Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), Earth observation technology.
Mains: Application of space technology in disaster early warning, inter-agency communication challenges, and regional disaster management mechanisms.
news.upsc_analysis: Space-based Earth observation provides unprecedented accuracy in tracking land deformation and hydrological changes. However, as demonstrated by this incident, technical capability must be coupled with robust operational channels, standardized data-sharing agreements, and last-mile early warning systems to convert remote sensing data into saved lives.
challenges: Integrating complex satellite observation streams into real-time operational disaster response.
Cross-border data sharing and inter-agency alerting delays during rapidly evolving natural hazards.
way_forward: Establish automated, real-time alerts linking space research centers with national disaster management authorities.
Strengthen regional cross-border early warning protocols for neighboring vulnerable countries.
news.mains_notes:
### Role of Earth Observation in Disaster Risk Reduction
* **Capability:** Advanced radar payloads on satellites offer all-weather, day-and-night surface deformation and hazard mapping.
* **Systemic Challenge:** Converting satellite observations into actionable early warnings requires streamlined data processing, automated risk thresholds, and reliable field dissemination.
mains_questions: Examine the potential and limitations of Earth observation satellites in regional disaster early-warning systems. How can space-faring nations improve last-mile alert mechanisms?
Highlight the key features of joint space collaborations such as the Indo-US satellite program in enhancing environmental monitoring in South Asia.
news.takeaway: A $1.3 billion joint Indo-US satellite recorded signs of an impending disaster in Nepal, demonstrating advanced satellite capability while highlighting gaps in early-warning dissemination.
prelims_facts: The joint Indo-US Earth observation satellite project involves an investment of $1.3 billion.
Radar-based Earth observation satellites can monitor surface changes independent of cloud cover and daylight conditions.

hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### भारत-अमेरिका उपग्रह और आपदा पूर्व चेतावनी

भारत और संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका के 1.3 अरब डॉलर लागत वाले एक संयुक्त पृथ्वी अवलोकन उपग्रह ने नेपाल में प्राकृतिक आपदा आने से पहले ही उससे जुड़े शुरुआती पर्यावरणीय संकेतों को दर्ज कर लिया था। आधुनिक सेंसर द्वारा इन परिवर्तनों को रिकॉर्ड किए जाने के बावजूद, परिचालन स्तर पर समय रहते चेतावनी प्रसारित नहीं की जा सकी।

### मुख्य बिंदु
* **मिशन लागत और सहयोग:** यह उपग्रह भारत और अमेरिका के बीच 1.3 अरब डॉलर का एक प्रमुख संयुक्त पृथ्वी-अवलोकन प्रयास है।
* **आपदा पहचान:** उपग्रह के उन्नत राडार उपकरणों ने नेपाल में आपदा आने से पहले ही धरातलीय परिवर्तनों का खाका खींच लिया था।
* **चेतावनी तंत्र में अंतर:** यह घटना अंतरिक्ष आधारित अवलोकन और आपदा प्रबंधन प्राधिकरणों के बीच त्वरित संपर्क तथा डेटा साझाकरण में सुधार की आवश्यकता को रेखांकित करती है।

news.headline: Rivalry among TMC factions in focus as parties gear up for Bengal civic polls
news.story_lead: Rivalry among TMC factions in focus as parties gear up for Bengal civic polls West Bengal civic polls are set to see a contest involving rival Trinamool Congress factions, the BJP and Congress as parties prepare for elections in Kolkata and Howrah. Rivalry between the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (MAITC), the Democratic Trinamool Congress (DTC) and the faction of Trinamool MPs who have joined the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) intensified on Friday as parties in West Bengal geared up for the municipal elections scheduled for Kolkata and Howrah in November. The parties said poll notifications were likely to be issued within a few days, leaving little time for candidate selection and campaigning.

Rivalry between the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (MAITC), the Democratic Trinamool Congress (DTC) and the faction of Trinamool MPs who have joined the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) intensified on Friday as parties in West Bengal geared up for the municipal elections scheduled for Kolkata and Howrah in November. The parties said poll notifications were likely to be issued within a few days, leaving little time for candidate selection and campaigning. “Local leaders loyal to Mamata Banerjee will receive priority during candidate selection. There may be some talks on seat adjustment with the Congress if the situation demands but it is too early to speak on that,” a leader from the Mamata camp said, requesting anonymity after a meeting at the former chief minister’s residence in Kalighat. “Although Congress state committees select municipal poll nominees, issues such as alliances are decided by our central leaders. No such talks have taken place so far,” Pradesh Congress general secretary Asutosh Chatterjee said. Kunal Ghosh, a Kolkata MLA from the Mamata faction, targeted the NCPI, a self-declared ally of the Bharatiya Janata Party-led National Democratic Alliance government. Ghosh posted a photo of wall graffiti in which the face of Kolkata North Lok Sabha member Sudip Bandopadhyay — the leader of the Trinamool MPs who joined the NCPI — was covered with black paint. In the graffiti found in a neighbourhood in Shyambazar, Bandopadhyay was flanked by Union home minister Amit Shah and state BJP president Samik Bhattacharya. The graffiti featuring the two BJP leaders was untouched. “I don’t know who disfigured the graffiti but whoever did should not spare the other traitors in our party,” Ghosh said. The DTC, led by Ritabrata Banerjee, announced that it would not form an alliance with the NCPI. “We are the real Trinamool. We will contest on our own,” DTC president Arup Roy said after a party meeting. On October 20, the 20 former Trinamool MPs in the NCPI sought more time from Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla to respond to petitions filed by the MAITC seeking their disqualification from the Lower House. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which controls 209 of Bengal’s 294 Assembly seats, held its first preparatory meeting in the presence of central leaders in Kolkata on Friday. “Our candidates will be selected based on their proven performance. People from other parties will not be entertained,” said Union minister of state Sukanta Majumdar, who is heading the BJP’s election committee for the Kolkata polls. The NCPI had earlier expressed eagerness to contest the civic body polls as a BJP ally, but Majumdar said his party would contest all the seats. On Friday, Majumdar also ruled out fielding Trinamool councillors who won the last election if they switched camps now. The civic bodies in both Kolkata and Howrah are being run by state-appointed administrators. The Trinamool councillors and the mayor resigned in Kolkata in May following the party’s defeat to the BJP in the Assembly polls. No election has been held in the Howrah Municipal Corporation since 2018 because of complications arising from delimitation rules. “The BJP will not have allies. Our candidates will contest all seats,” Ritesh Tiwari, co-convenor of the BJP’s four-member poll committee for Kolkata, told HT. In August this year, the West Bengal Legislative Assembly passed two bills to increase the number of civic wards from 144 to 209 in the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) area and from 50 to 68 under the Howrah Municipal Corporation’s (HMC) jurisdiction. Presenting the bills in the Assembly, state urban development and municipal affairs minister Agnimitra Paul said delimitation would create smaller wards with lower populations, making the delivery of civic services to citizens faster and easier. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Tanmay Chatterjee Tanmay Chatterjee has spent more than three decades covering regional and national politics, internal security, intelligence, defence and corruption. news.headline: Tragic Collision on Jaipur-Ajmer Highway Claims 3 Lives, Injures 7 Maharashtra Pilgrims
news.story_lead: Three pilgrims from Maharashtra were killed on the spot and seven others sustained injuries when their bus collided with a trailer on the Jaipur-Ajmer National Highway in Rajasthan's Jaipur district. The bus was carrying 28 devotees who were traveling toward Chittorgarh after visiting the Khatushyamji shrine.
news.full_article_text:
In a tragic road accident in the early hours of Saturday around 1:50 AM, three pilgrims lost their lives and seven others were injured on the Jaipur-Ajmer National Highway near the Bagru area in Jaipur district. A private bus carrying 28 pilgrims from Nashik, Maharashtra, collided with a trailer while descending the Bagru culvert. Local police reported that the trailer was on fire at the time of the collision.

The group of devotees was traveling from the Khatushyamji temple to the Sanwariya Seth (Sanwalia Seth) temple located in Chittorgarh. Due to the impact, passengers seated in the front section of the bus suffered serious injuries. Local residents along with police personnel conducted rescue operations to extract those trapped in the wreckage. The deceased were identified as Mahendra (38), Sandeep (45), and Deepak (47).

All seven injured individuals were rushed to the trauma facility at Sawai Man Singh (SMS) Hospital in Jaipur for medical treatment. According to medical authorities, two of the injured were admitted in critical condition, three were kept under close observation, and two were discharged after receiving first aid. Police under Bagru Station House Officer Chandrabhan have launched an investigation into the precise cause of the accident.

In a separate incident on the preceding Friday around 6:00 AM, four friends from Agra, Uttar Pradesh, were killed and two others injured when their car plunged into a ditch following a tyre burst on National Highway 148 (Dausa-Manoharpur) in the Raisar area of Jaipur district. The victims were also returning from the Khatushyamji shrine.
bullet_points: A bus carrying 28 pilgrims from Nashik collided with a trailer on the Jaipur-Ajmer National Highway at Bagru culvert.
Three pilgrims—Mahendra (38), Sandeep (45), and Deepak (47)—died on the spot.
Seven injured passengers were transported to the trauma center at SMS Hospital in Jaipur.
The pilgrims were traveling to the Sanwariya Seth temple in Chittorgarh after visiting Khatushyamji.
Bagru police reported that the trailer involved in the collision was on fire at the time of the crash.
In another crash on Friday on NH-148, four Agra residents died after a tyre burst sent their car into a ditch near Raisar.
key_facts: Incident Location: Bagru culvert on Jaipur-Ajmer National Highway, Jaipur district, Rajasthan.
Pilgrims Origin and Route: Devotees from Nashik, Maharashtra, traveling from Khatushyamji to Sanwariya Seth Temple in Chittorgarh.
Fatalities and Injuries: 3 deceased (Mahendra, Sandeep, Deepak) and 7 injured treated at SMS Hospital.
Secondary Accident: Tyre burst on NH-148 near Raisar killed 4 Agra residents returning from Khatushyamji.
important_dates: 2026-10-24 (Date of Bagru highway bus collision)
2026-10-23 (Date of Raisar car crash following tyre burst)
exam_relevance: Illustrates critical issues concerning national highway road safety, emergency trauma services, and traffic incident management in India.
news.upsc_analysis: Road traffic accidents remain a major safety and administrative concern on Indian highways. The incident underscores the imperative of strict vehicular fitness compliance, effective highway hazard removal, and timely trauma medical care. Policies targeting black-spot identification, prompt removal of disabled or burning highway vehicles, and strict enforcement of speed limits and maintenance norms are vital for curbing highway fatalities.
causes: Bus collision with a burning trailer during a highway culvert descent.
Tyre burst leading to loss of vehicle control in the secondary Raisar incident.
impacts: Loss of seven lives across two road accidents in Jaipur district within a 24-hour window.
Injuries to seven pilgrims requiring emergency medical and trauma care.
challenges: Managing late-night highway hazards and prompt clearance of distressed vehicles.
Enforcing strict vehicle fitness and tyre safety checks for long-distance pilgrim travel.
government_steps: Police deployment for rescue operations and official investigation into crash causes.
Immediate trauma care provided at SMS Hospital under senior medical supervision.
constitutional_or_policy_link: Relevant to the implementation of the Motor Vehicles Act, National Road Safety Policy, and emergency medical response protocols.
way_forward: Strengthening night-time highway patrolling and automated hazard alerts.
Establishing faster vehicle clearance mechanisms for broken-down or burning vehicles on national highways.
Upgrading regional trauma care response along busy traffic corridors.
news.mains_notes: Road safety in India requires comprehensive policy interventions focusing on the '4 Es': Engineering of roads, Engineering of vehicles, Enforcement of traffic laws, and Emergency care. High fatality rates on national highways highlight gaps in vehicle safety checks and delayed hazard mitigation.
mains_questions: Examine the key factors contributing to high road accident fatalities on Indian national highways and suggest policy measures for mitigation.
Discuss the critical role of the 'Golden Hour' and trauma care infrastructure in reducing mortality from highway accidents in India.
news.takeaway: A road crash on the Jaipur-Ajmer highway claimed three lives and injured seven pilgrims from Maharashtra, drawing attention to road safety and hazard management on major transit corridors.

Sanwariya Seth (Sanwalia Seth) temple is located in Chittorgarh district, Rajasthan.
National Highway 148 links Dausa and Manoharpur in Rajasthan.

hindi_translation.headline: जयपुर-अजमेर हाईवे पर भीषण हादसा: महाराष्ट्र के 3 श्रद्धालुओं की मौत, 7 घायल
hindi_translation.story_lead: राजस्थान के जयपुर जिले में जयपुर-अजमेर राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग पर श्रद्धालुओं से भरी एक बस के ट्रॉले से टकरा जाने से महाराष्ट्र के तीन श्रद्धालुओं की मौके पर ही मौत हो गई और सात अन्य घायल हो गए। बस में 28 श्रद्धालु सवार थे जो खाटूश्यामजी के दर्शन के बाद चित्तौड़गढ़ जा रहे थे।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
शनिवार तड़के करीब 1:50 बजे जयपुर जिले के बगरू क्षेत्र में जयपुर-अजमेर राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग पर एक दर्दनाक सड़क हादसा हुआ, जिसमें तीन श्रद्धालुओं की मौत हो गई और सात अन्य घायल हो गए। महाराष्ट्र के नासिक से 28 श्रद्धालुओं को ले जा रही एक निजी बस बगरू पुलिया से उतरते समय एक ट्रॉले से टकरा गई। पुलिस के अनुसार, टक्कर के समय ट्रॉले में आग लगी हुई थी।

श्रद्धालुओं का दल खाटूश्यामजी मंदिर के दर्शन के बाद चित्तौड़गढ़ स्थित सांवलिया सेठ मंदिर जा रहा था। टक्कर इतनी तेज थी कि बस के अगले हिस्से में बैठे यात्रियों को गंभीर चोटें आईं। स्थानीय निवासियों और पुलिसकर्मियों ने बचाव अभियान चलाकर मलबे में फंसे लोगों को बाहर निकाला। मृतकों की पहचान महेंद्र (38), संदीप (45) और दीपक (47) के रूप में हुई है।

सभी सात घायलों को इलाज के लिए जयपुर के सवाई मानसिंह (एसएमएस) अस्पताल के ट्रॉमा सेंटर में भर्ती कराया गया। चिकित्सा अधिकारियों के अनुसार, दो घायलों की हालत नाजुक होने के कारण उन्हें भर्ती किया गया, तीन को निगरानी वार्ड में रखा गया और दो को प्राथमिक उपचार के बाद छुट्टी दे दी गई। बगरू थानाधिकारी चंद्रभान के नेतृत्व में पुलिस ने हादसे के कारणों की जांच शुरू कर दी है।

एक अन्य घटना में, शुक्रवार सुबह करीब 6:00 बजे जयपुर जिले के रायसर क्षेत्र में राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग 148 (दौसा-मनोहरपुर) पर टायर फटने के बाद कार खाई में गिरने से उत्तर प्रदेश के आगरा के चार दोस्तों की मौत हो गई और दो अन्य घायल हो गए। ये सभी भी खाटूश्यामजी के दर्शन कर लौट रहे थे।
bullet_points: नासिक से 28 श्रद्धालुओं को ले जा रही एक बस बगरू पुलिया पर जयपुर-अजमेर हाईवे पर एक ट्रॉले से टकरा गई।
हादसे में तीन श्रद्धालुओं—महेंद्र (38), संदीप (45) और दीपक (47) की मौके पर ही मौत हो गई।
सात घायल यात्रियों को जयपुर के एसएमएस अस्पताल के ट्रॉमा सेंटर में भर्ती कराया गया।
श्रद्धालु खाटूश्यामजी के दर्शन के बाद चित्तौड़गढ़ स्थित सांवलिया सेठ मंदिर जा रहे थे।
बगरू पुलिस ने बताया कि टक्कर के समय दुर्घटनाग्रस्त ट्रॉले में आग लगी हुई थी।
शुक्रवार को एनएच-148 पर रायसर के पास टायर फटने से हुई एक अन्य कार दुर्घटना में आगरा के चार लोगों की मौत हो गई।

static_gk: Reserve Bank of India (RBI): Established on April 1, 1935, under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
Headquarters: Mumbai, Maharashtra.
Core Function: Functions as India's central bank, regulating monetary policy, financial institutions, foreign exchange, and currency issuance.
news.headline: Strong Macroeconomic Fundamentals Anchor India's Economy Against Global Headwinds: RBI Bulletin
news.story_lead: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has highlighted in its bulletin that strong domestic macroeconomic fundamentals continue to anchor the Indian economy. This strong foundation provides resilience against persistent global headwinds and international economic uncertainties.
news.full_article_text:
### Macroeconomic Fundamentals and Economic Resilience

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) noted in its publication that India's domestic economic framework remains strong, serving as an effective anchor during periods of international market instability.

* **Domestic Anchor:** Solid internal macroeconomic fundamentals help insulate the Indian economy from external spillovers and global uncertainties.
* **Global Environment:** Adverse international economic conditions and volatile external market forces continue to create headwinds, but domestic stability offers significant buffer support.
* **Central Bank Assessment:** The RBI's assessment underlines the importance of maintaining key domestic economic indicators to sustain long-term stability and resilience.
bullet_points: The RBI released its bulletin assessing the current state of the Indian economy.
Strong domestic macroeconomic fundamentals serve as an anchor against global headwinds.
International markets face ongoing economic uncertainties and external challenges.
Domestic economic strength provides buffer capacity against global financial volatility.
key_facts: Report Source: RBI Bulletin.
Core Finding: India's macroeconomic fundamentals anchor the economy against international headwinds.
important_dates: 2026-10-24: Publication date of the coverage on the RBI Bulletin.
exam_relevance: Prelims: Institutional role of RBI, macroeconomic indicators, monetary stability concepts.
Mains: GS Paper III (Indian Economy) - Economic growth, external sector resilience, and macroeconomic policy.
news.upsc_analysis: The RBI Bulletin highlights the buffer capability of strong domestic macroeconomic fundamentals in safeguarding an emerging market economy against external shocks and global demand fluctuations.
causes: Global economic volatility and international financial uncertainty.
impacts: Enhanced resilience of the domestic economy against global spillovers and external shocks.
challenges: Navigating persistent external headwinds and global macroeconomic uncertainties.
way_forward: Sustain prudent monetary management and domestic economic activity to maintain resilience against global economic pressures.
news.mains_notes: Macroeconomic fundamentals—including stable internal demand and effective monetary policy—serve as a critical defense line for an economy facing global volatility. Understanding how domestic economic indicators counter external shocks is vital for analyzing India's economic growth path.
mains_questions: Analyze how robust domestic macroeconomic fundamentals shield an economy from adverse global headwinds, with reference to the Reserve Bank of India's recent observations.
Discuss the strategic importance of internal economic buffers in maintaining economic stability during periods of international market volatility.
news.takeaway: India's solid macroeconomic fundamentals provide vital stability against global economic uncertainty and adverse external pressures.
prelims_facts: The RBI Bulletin provides periodic assessments of the Indian economy and macroeconomic indicators.
Strong macroeconomic fundamentals buffer domestic activity against international headwinds.

hindi_translation.headline: मजबूत समष्टि आर्थिक बुनियादी ढांचे से वैश्विक प्रतिकूल परिस्थितियों के बीच भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था को मिला आधार: आरबीआई बुलेटिन
hindi_translation.story_lead: भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक (आरबीआई) ने अपने बुलेटिन में कहा है कि मजबूत घरेलू समष्टि आर्थिक बुनियादी ढांचे भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था को स्थिरता प्रदान कर रहे हैं। यह मजबूत आधार वैश्विक अनिश्चितताओं और प्रतिकूल परिस्थितियों के बीच देश को मजबूती देता है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### समष्टि आर्थिक बुनियादी ढांचा और आर्थिक मजबूती

भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक (आरबीआई) ने अपने प्रकाशन में उल्लेख किया है कि भारत का घरेलू आर्थिक ढांचा मजबूत बना हुआ है, जो अंतरराष्ट्रीय बाजार की अस्थिरता के दौरान एक प्रभावी आधार के रूप में कार्य करता है।

* **घरेलू आधार:** ठोस आंतरिक समष्टि आर्थिक बुनियादी ढांचे भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था को बाहरी झटकों और वैश्विक अनिश्चितताओं से बचाने में मदद करते हैं।
* **वैश्विक परिवेश:** प्रतिकूल अंतरराष्ट्रीय आर्थिक स्थितियां और अस्थिर बाहरी कारक चुनौतियां पेश कर रहे हैं, लेकिन घरेलू स्थिरता महत्वपूर्ण सुरक्षा प्रदान करती है।
* **केंद्रीय बैंक का आकलन:** आरबीआई का आकलन दीर्घकालिक स्थिरता और मजबूती बनाए रखने के लिए प्रमुख घरेलू आर्थिक संकेतकों को बनाए रखने के महत्व पर जोर देता है।
bullet_points: आरबीआई ने भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था की स्थिति का आकलन करते हुए अपना बुलेटिन जारी किया।
मजबूत घरेलू समष्टि आर्थिक बुनियादी ढांचे वैश्विक प्रतिकूल परिस्थितियों के खिलाफ आधार प्रदान करते हैं।
अंतरराष्ट्रीय बाजार निरंतर आर्थिक अनिश्चितताओं और बाहरी चुनौतियों का सामना कर रहे हैं।

hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### एशियाई पैरा खेल 2026 प्रदर्शन अवलोकन

एशियाई पैरा खेल 2026 भारत सहित प्रतिभागी एशियाई देशों के प्रदर्शन मानकों और पदक उपलब्धियों को प्रस्तुत करता है।

* **पदक ट्रैकिंग**: तालिका विभिन्न खेल श्रेणियों में भारतीय एथलीटों द्वारा हासिल किए गए स्वर्ण, रजत और कांस्य पदकों का विस्तृत कवरेज प्रदान करती है।
* **एथलेटिक प्रतिनिधित्व**: भारतीय दल विभिन्न खेल स्पर्धाओं में सक्रिय रूप से भाग लेता है, जो राष्ट्रीय पैरा-खेल प्रशासन और एथलीट प्रशिक्षण कार्यक्रमों में प्रगति को दर्शाता है।
bullet_points: 2026 एशियाई पैरा खेल भाग लेने वाले देशों की पदक उपलब्धियों को ट्रैक करते हैं।
भारत के प्रदर्शन को स्वर्ण, रजत और कांस्य पदकों की एक व्यापक तालिका के माध्यम से सूचीबद्ध किया गया है।
प्रतियोगिता में पूरे एशिया के एथलीटों के लिए तैयार की गई विभिन्न खेल स्पर्धाएं शामिल हैं।
